title: Late-bound batching checkins - weekly journal
content:
Purpose
Weekly capture of small experiments, standup blurbs, and oddball observations for the late-bound batching project (kv-cache interactions + throttle heuristics). This is intended as a fast-moving team scratchpad that the oncall can skim before handoff.

Summary (top-level)
- We continue to see a small p99 tail increase (~8–12ms) when late-bound batches are stitched across heterogenous kernels under shadow sampling traffic (small concurrent sessions).
- Two candidate mitigations: (1) micro-throttle per-queue to avoid kernel context churn, and (2) opportunistic coalescing with KV prefix alignment.
- Eviction pressure on cold-KV lanes spikes during synthetic reroute tests (JIRA SRV-2719).

Attendees / quick notes from 2029-11-07 standup
- Maya C. (lead): rapid sync, asked for clarity on which metric to normalize — using tokens/sec per-GPU for throughput and p50/p99 for latency.
- Ethan R.: landed initial micro-throttle patch (GH redwood/serve#4821) behind a flag; instrumented per-queue backoff counter.
- Priya K.: collected prefilling traces from dedicated pool beta; found correlating spike with our re-orderer when sequence_len < 64.
- Noah W.: wrote harness to replay production-sampled requests but with artificial fragment alignment to stress stitch paths.

Experiment logs (short, reproducible)
1) Micro-throttle (flag: throttle_micro_v1) — 2029-11-06 run
- Method: ramped 10k requests over 10 minutes against a 4-GPU dedicated pool. Compared baseline (no micro-throttle) vs enabled.
- Observations: p50 unchanged, p95 slightly improved (~3%), p99 increased in a subset of runs where prefetch occupancy hit 90%.
- Hypothesis: micro-throttle reduces queue head-of-line jitter but increases kernel handoff when throttles misfire (backoff-unblock ripple).
- Next: add jitter-smoothing (randomized backoff windows) and re-run.

2) Opportunistic coalesce with KV prefix alignment (flag: coalesce_kv_align_v0) — 2029-11-08 run
- Method: when two requests are close in arrival time and share first-32-token prefix hash we attempt same-batch placement even if late-bound decision would normally separate them.
- Observations: throughput +5–7% on small prompts, p99 improved by 6ms on shadow traffic. However we saw a small regression on quality for a narrow prompt family where prefixes are common but tail tokens diverge.
- Decision: disable quality-sensitive coalesce on routes tagged "strict-output". Add sampling to measure downstream quality impact.

3) KV eviction pressure replay — 2029-11-09 synthetic stress
- Method: replayed a 30min window of reroute-heavy traffic that previously triggered thrash in prod.
- Observations: cold-KV lanes (recently-created sessions) experienced 3x higher miss rates when late-bound batching triggered kernel swaps. Memory spike correlated with duplicate prefetch windows.
- Action: reduced duplicate prefetch window from 400ms -> 200ms; immediate drop in duplicate prefetches by ~60%.

Profiling snippets / notable numbers
- Baseline p50 / p95 / p99 for the test harness under 4xA100 equivalent: 12ms / 36ms / 120ms. With coalesce_kv_align_v0: p50 unchanged, p95 34ms, p99 114ms.
- Micro-throttle runs: observed scheduler context-switches up 18% when throttle enabled; suggests we are shifting cost to kernel rescheduling.
- KV cache miss-rate (cold lanes) peaked at 27% during synthetic reroute; after decreasing duplicate prefetch: 11%.

Open oddities observed this week
- Intermittent ~1–2s stall on one GPU during long blocks when a late-bound batch exceeds sequence_len 2048 — only repros with shadow-sampling of multi-turn chat. Root cause unknown (scheduling priority inversion suspected).
- One instance where coalescing tied two sessions with same prefix but different tool-calls; downstream tool-caller saw malformed structured output. We need route-level policy to opt-out.

Decisions / temporary mitigations
- Flip coalesce_kv_align_v0 on for non-strict routes in beta only; production rollout gated on quality sampling results. (Owner: Priya, due 2029-11-14)
- Roll back micro-throttle for global fleet; keep patch in staging and iterate on jitter smoothing + reschedule cost analysis. (Owner: Ethan, due 2029-11-12)
- Reduce duplicate prefetch window to 200ms across dedicated pools. (Owner: Noah, deployed 2029-11-09)

Action items (who / what / when)
- Priya: set up automated quality sampling for coalesce experiments (10k sampled outputs vs baseline) and attach eval dashboard. Due: 2029-11-14. Linked: Confluence page.
- Ethan: implement randomized jitter backoff and run micro-throttle A/B with scheduler traces; attach flamegraphs. Due: 2029-11-12.
- Noah: investigate the 1–2s stall reproducer — capture kernel logs, isolate whether NVML or batch allocation is responsible. Due: 2029-11-11.
- Maya: add a short checklist to the oncall playbook explaining when to disable coalescing and how to tag routes as "strict-output". Due: 2029-11-13.

Risks and escalations
- Quality regressions from prefix-based coalesce are subtle — could silently affect customers with structured-output flows. We must not roll this change wide without paired evals.
- Kernel priority inversion stall could affect SLAs if it impacts the tail for sustained multi-turn chat workloads. If Noah's investigation indicates scheduler bugs, we escalate to infra and SRE.

Questions for next sync
- If micro-throttle reduces p95 but increases p99, can we accept that tradeoff with a per-route config? Which routes should be exempt?
- Is a hybrid approach feasible: micro-throttle only for kernels with < X context-switch/sec?

Notes to self / informal
- Keep tiny experiment names consistent: micro-throttle v1/v2, coalesce_kv_align v0/v1, prefetch_dup_window_{ms}.
- Don't forget to annotate GH PRs with the exact test harness commit id used for numbers — reproducibility is failing us sometimes because harness changes silently.
- Quick tip: when replaying production traces for prefix coalesce, mask user tokens to avoid PII leakage.

Appendix: short command snippets used this week
- Start harness: ./test-harness --trace-id replay-20291106 --concurrency 200 --profile=kv
- Dump per-queue stats: ./queue-inspect --pool dedicated-beta --since 2029-11-06T00:00Z > qstats.txt

End of week note
We have interesting leads that move the needle but each fix currently trades one tail metric for another (or quality). Priority for next week: get the coalesce quality-sample pipeline running and collect scheduler traces for micro-throttle runs. If both look good, we can try a narrow canary on light-traffic routes.

-- Maya
